thread:
maya: Heads-up — on the long-context replay job (seq len ~12k) I'm seeing steady mem growth on the KV cache and a sharp fragmentation spike after ~30m. Heap profile attached in-line.
maya: Alloc histogram (hot buckets):
```
slot_size  count
256        1.2M
512        420k
1024       80k
```
Context: workload mixes short chat continuations with occasional very long prompts.

sam: ugh. is this the same pattern as the stress-run last month or a new shape? any allocation churn trace? :thinking:

maya: Different. last month had churn from tiny ephemeral entries. This one shows a few long-lived large entries that never get reused and block the buddy/free lists -> free fragmentation. profiler shows many slab holes where buddies don't align.

alex: can you paste the allocator counters? free-list depth / per-size free-run?

maya: quick dump: `free_runs[256]=120, free_runs[512]=5, free_runs[1024]=2, allocs_since_compact=1.8M`

kai: that ratio screams block-size mismatch. We tuned tiny chunks down to 256 to save tokens, but the long sequences allocate lots of 512/1024 KV pages. When those become sticky you get internal fragmentation.

sam: proposal: try widening mid buckets to 384/768 experimentally (non-power-of-two) or switch to a multi-class binning that considers contiguous KV chain length. Tradeoff: more metadata but fewer wasted bytes.

alex: alternative: opportunistic compaction — background pass that tries to coalesce free neighbors incrementally without stopping allocations. Credit-limited so tail latency stays bounded. I sketched a pseudo-op:

```
for i in 0..credits_per_cycle:
  block = pick_candidate_from_holemap()
  if block.can_merge_with(peer):
    merge(block, peer)
```

Keep credits tied to p50 CPU to avoid hurting hot threads.

maya: +1 for background merging. We saw earlier compaction pauses when we tried full-slab GC. This credit approach might be safer. Also want per-tenant eviction hysteresis — long contexts from a few tenants shouldn't starve others.

kai: note on latency: merging can cause small transient stalls if we move pointers under lock. Consider lock-free handover: mark->migrate->switch-pointer technique. More complex but smoother.

sam: on block-size tuning: I'd rather we run an A/B on dedicated canary nodes: one with 512-min-block, one with mixed 256/384 buckets, one with compactor enabled. Capture p50/p95 tail and memory growth over 2h.

maya: i'll bake the canary images. checklist:
- patch allocator to emit `holemap_gap_ratio` metric
- compactor credit config (default 1000/cycle)
- per-tenant eviction threshold label
- lightweight test harness that replays the long-context trace

alex: small nit — make sure compactor respects KV cache TTLs and doesn't try to compact entries that are actively pinned by decoders (use pinned bit).

dev-bot: Canary build queued: `ci/kv-compact/canary-3740001234` — tests: unit, memprofile, longtrace-replay (estimated 22m).

sam: perfect. after we get metrics let's graph: memory_used, fragmentation_ratio, tail_latencies, compaction_cpu. if fragmentation_ratio drops while p95 stable -> winner.

maya: timeline: aim to run canaries tomorrow morning and collect 3x 2h runs. I'll post results in this thread.

kai: cc @alex if you can lend the lockless migration prototype for the canary, will speed iteration.

alex: yup, will push a lightweight version (no full correctness sweep) that should be safe behind a feature flag.

maya: thanks all — going to start instrumenting now. will ping when build is up. :thumbsup:
